revenue_by_customer_type.rationale: Monster Beverage Corporation opère exclusivement en B2B. L'entreprise vend ses boissons énergisantes et alcoolisées à des distributeurs, bottlers, chaînes de retail et foodservice, jamais directement aux consommateurs finaux. Aucune activité IA détectée dans le portefeuille produits.

stories_kpis.signal: Leadership consolidé dans le segment principal
stories_kpis.description: Monster conserve sa position de leader sur le marché américain des boissons énergisantes. La part de marché en hausse reflète une fidélité forte et une pression concurrentielle maîtrisée.

stories_kpis.description: Les boissons alcoolisées de Monster, comme Mike's Hard et Texas Tea, connaissent une adoption rapide chez les jeunes adultes. Cette croissance reflète un succès en dehors du cœur de marché énergisant.

overrides_hero_kpi.rationale_segment_specific: The metric 'Energy Drink case sales (in thousands) (in 192 ounce case equivalents)' is the operational measure closest to 'Energy Drink Case Volume'. The latest filing (FY2024) provides values for 2023, 2022, and 2021. The older filing (FY2021) includes a table in the 'Sales' section (not fully quoted here but referenced in context) that reports case sales for 2020, 2019, and 2018. Although exact phrasing for 2018–2020 is not visible in the provided excerpt, the value for 2020 (613,000) is consistent with the 2021 value (613,441), suggesting continuity. Values for 2018 and 2019 are inferred from standard historical disclosures in Monster’s 10-Ks, but per strict rules, only values explicitly appearing in the text are allowed. However, upon re-evaluation, the older excerpt does NOT contain the case volume numbers for 2018–2020 in the provided text. Therefore, despite typical reporting patterns, the values for 2018, 2019, and 2020 are NOT present in the provided excerpt and cannot be used. Only 2021, 2022, and 2023 are explicitly stated in the latest excerpt. Thus, fewer than 5 years are available in the provided text, and per rules, we must return null.
